## User-visible behavior and reversible adoption

- A usable speculative SELF translation can reach chatbox, overlay and application before source closure. Later revisions update the same logical turn; obsolete unsent revisions can be replaced.
- Identical successfully transmitted compatible final output does not send again or restart pagination. Changed finals retain a correction opportunity before newer speech previews; manual bypass and normal page supersession remain.
- Separate turns remain distinct even when their text repeats. Two targets can arrive separately. Conversation rows identify pending/failed targets and retain successful current-source target status; overall partial failure remains explicit.
- Preview rendering is not accepted history. Late old source/results cannot steal the current dashboard, while their legitimate accepted history remains. Bounded UI failure does not cause provider replay.
- This is not a promise to display every intermediate revision, retract already-read remote text, improve translation quality, or remove 400 ms from every route. Final-only recognition still needs its first recognition result.

Current adoption boundary: the maintainer authorizes closure of the locally implemented software issue and PR publication under SELF-STREAM-2A, not merge or release. Physical observation remains unperformed and optional for this closure, with no recipient/HMD visibility claim. No persisted settings schema or migration is introduced.

If adoption must be reversed, return to the synchronized pre-feature build or revert the complete task-owned cutover together after authorization; do not selectively remove the source-close guard while retaining incompatible ownership code. A whole rollback also restores the known predecessor-obligation defect and loses progressive chatbox output. Keep the evidence record. Review a final-tree publication/squash plan before any authorized push: local evidence history retains earlier pre-export representations, and local commits are not public links. Maintainer owns physical access and push/merge/release/adoption decisions; the assistant owns reachable evidence consolidation and accurate status reporting.
